title: Bare build prompt -- material AND geometry richness without elicitation
//: Material/geometry-richness P0 headroom scenario (docs/agentic-redesign/73-creative-richness-design.md). A truly bare prompt -- no 'make it look nice' nudge -- against the shipping empty starter scene. Measures whether the agent reaches for spatially-varying painters, the scalar-pipe, and non-primitive geometry verbs on an unprompted build, without ever blocking on style questions (askUserMax tolerates at most one ask; ask_user stays reserved for material/subject AMBIGUITY per build_ambiguous_scene, not style taste). objects_reaching_kinds is a MEASUREMENT, not an anti-adversarial gate -- it defeats a single-decoy gaming pattern (all diversity bound to one hidden object) but a determined multi-decoy scene can still pass every CST-side checkpoint here; the render-side closer is the deferred A2/P3 detector. Geometry checkpoints (geometry_kinds/advanced_geometry) have NO reachability guard at all -- a tiny decoy chunk per missing kind satisfies them; disclosed deliberately rather than papered over, since requiring 2+ advanced-geometry objects would over-prescribe legitimate scenes. Render ceiling recalibrated 0.35->0.9 after the first baseline: courtyards are OUTDOOR scenes and gemini legitimately renders them at meanLuma 0.67-0.82; the ceiling exists to catch blown-out exposure (~1.0), not daylight. Object ceiling 40->100 after baseline v2: a 50-object, 7-painter-kind courtyard is ambition, not runaway (budgets catch true runaways).

budgets.//: Matches the furnished build-scenario family (build_ambiguous_scene et al). Deliberately loose: a budget-exhausted run would be indistinguishable from the flat-materials signal this scenario exists to measure; efficiency stays visible via the report's toolCalls/wall columns.

checkpoints.//: Measurement, not a gate (see the scenario-level comment above). Taste-blind: ANY non-excluded painter counts however crude -- a scalar_painter bound to a flat 0.7 with zero spatial variation scores identically to a genuinely varied microsurface; this op cannot see the difference. Decoy caveats are inherited from distinct_chunk_kinds/objects_reaching_kinds above, and this op's own gap is STRICTLY WORSE than either: unlike objects_reaching_kinds, param_binding has NO reachability filter at all -- an ORPHANED material (bound to a painter but referenced by zero standard_object, zero geometry, not even a hidden 0.001-unit decoy box) still counts. A one-line, never-instantiated ggx_material with alphax bound to a scalar_painter satisfies this checkpoint on its own; objects_reaching_kinds' render-side closer (deferred A2/P3) does not cover this op either, since there may be no object to reach in the first place. Arc-75 S2.3: a scaffold-expanded material (insert_material_scaffold's tmpl_<name>_mat) legitimately satisfies this checkpoint -- expansion-driven richness is NOT a decoy or a gaming pattern, it is the mechanism S2 exists to encourage. Read this count TOGETHER with the chunk_name_prefix_count checkpoint below (metricLabel 'scaffold_expanded'): the two are never summed, but side by side they split expansion-driven microsurface variation from hand-authored microsurface variation.

Arc-75 S2.3 provenance metric. PURE metric, never gates (weight 0, min 0 passes vacuously on any document, including one with zero scaffold calls) -- the kill rules read the trend on this label across runs, not a pass/fail here. Counts chunks named tmpl_<name>_<role> -- the insert_material_scaffold naming convention -- so scaffold_expanded is expansion count ONLY; it says nothing about whether the model then edited what the scaffold generated (propose_patch/set_param targeting a tmpl_* chunk). That post-expansion edit rate is the creativity signal and is measured from the TRAJECTORY (tool calls after the scaffold call), not from a checkpoint op -- there is deliberately no op for it here.

Arc-75 S3b.2 provenance metric. PURE metric, never gates (weight 0, min 0 passes vacuously, including on a document with zero geometry-scaffold calls -- these fixtures predate insert_geometry_scaffold, so this checkpoint reads 0 on both today by construction). Same tmpl_ convention as scaffold_expanded above, narrowed to category:'geometry' so it counts ONLY insert_geometry_scaffold's generated GEOMETRY chunks (box_geometry/sdf_geometry/sweep_geometry/displaced_geometry), not the whole expansion -- the geometry graph is 1-2 chunks per call, NOT 1-3: displaced_slab emits 3 tmpl_ chunks total but only 2 classify as category:'geometry' (box_geometry + displaced_geometry; its perlin2d_painter noise source is category:'painter' and is deliberately excluded here), while sweep_rail/blended_vessel/sdf_column each emit exactly 1 (sweep_geometry / sdf_geometry / sdf_geometry). Read this label TOGETHER with TWO others, never summed into either: scaffold_expanded above (which counts ALL tmpl_ chunks including materials/painters -- this label is the geometry-only subset of it) and advanced_geometry below (a scaffold-expanded sdf_geometry/sweep_geometry/displaced_geometry chunk satisfies advanced_geometry mechanically, since all four scaffold families terminate in one of those three kinds -- so a nonzero count here predicts a passing advanced_geometry, but advanced_geometry can also pass from hand-authored geometry with zero scaffold calls).
